heroHeadline: British Far-Right Commentator Milo Yiannopoulos Arrested by ICE
heroSubtitle: As of June 7, 2026, the $70 billion immigration enforcement reconciliation package — the largest such appropriation in U.S. history — passed by the Senate 52-47 on June 5 is heading to the House floor for a vote expected the week of June 8-12. On June 6, the New York Times published a major investigation confirming what TRAC data has long shown: ICE's own records contradict the administration's 'worst of the worst' characterization of its 73,000+ detainees, the majority of whom have no serious criminal conviction. The 287(g) program has now expanded to 1,903 active agreements — up from 688 when Trump took office. ICE's FY2026 detention death toll stands at 30+ deaths with Acting Director Venturella's June 4 memo ending post-release death reporting now in effect, eliminating a key accountability mechanism as the Delaney Hall hunger strike in Newark, NJ enters its third week with 300+ detainees still refusing food and labor. On June 5, a Rhode Island federal court issued the broadest travel ban ruling to date, vacating USCIS processing freezes for nationals of 39 countries entirely — rather than merely enjoining them. Combined with $45B+ in H.R. 1, total 2025-2026 immigration enforcement appropriations would exceed $115B — roughly 13× ICE's pre-2025 annual budget.
